cards.explanation: The answer is body. Joseph goes to Pilate, the governor, and asks for the body of Jesus (Matthew 27:58). That takes some nerve, friends, and I think it took a lot of love too. Pilate orders that the body be given to him.

The answer is True. Joseph takes the body and wraps it in a clean linen cloth (Matthew 27:59). The text gives us that detail right there, clean linen. I think that says Joseph handled the body with care.
The answer is His own new tomb, the one cut into the rock (Matthew 27:60). Think about that, friends. A rich man lays Jesus' body in a new tomb that's his own. I think that says a lot about Joseph.

The answer is stone. Joseph rolls a great stone across the entrance and goes away (Matthew 27:60). The text calls it great, and I'd guess he needed a good push. Nobody rolls a great stone by accident.
The answer is Mary Magdalene and the other Mary. They are sitting there opposite the tomb (Matthew 27:61). Joseph has gone away, but they stay. I think they're not ready to leave yet.

The answer is "After three days I will rise again." The chief priests and Pharisees say, "we remember that while He was alive that deceiver said, ‘After three days I will rise again.’" (Matthew 27:63) They call Him a deceiver, but they remember His words. That's what they bring to Pilate.

The answer is that His disciples steal Him away. The chief priests and Pharisees say, "Otherwise, His disciples may come and steal Him away and tell the people He has risen from the dead." (Matthew 27:64) That's their worry, spelled out, friends. They want the tomb secured until the third day.

The answer is True. Pilate says, "You have a guard…" and then, "Go, make the tomb as secure as you know how." (Matthew 27:65) He hands the job right back to them. I'd say that's a governor who is done with the whole conversation.

The answer is False. The text says the chief priests and Pharisees secured the tomb by sealing the stone and posting the guard (Matthew 27:66). Pilate had said, "You have a guard…" and they used it (Matthew 27:65). A sealed stone and a guard, all on purpose. And friends, the story isn't over.
